newsitem.title: FRANCE: UNIP reports French field peas damage after rain.
newsitem.headline: UNIP reports French field peas damage after rain.

text.p: Wet weather in June did some damage to the French field pea crop with farmers reporting unwanted germinations and leaf disease outbreaks in some regions, industry group UNIP said on Friday.
Rainy and windy conditions tilted crops over in some fields, which will hinder harvest progress while there was germination in areas where the crop had reached maturity, it said.
Spring peas in Poitou-Charentes, Aquitaine and the southeast and winter peas in northern France suffered most.
In the Normandy and Pas de Calais regions where the peas had developed less quickly high moisture levels sparked onbreaks of leaf disease.
UNIP predicted that yields in these regions will be below the "very high" yields reached last year.
One UNIP official said the Normandy area posted a yield of 5.62 tonnes per hectare last year and the Pas de Calais hit a record 6.3 tonnes.

But crops in the Beauce area in centre France and in the Champagne area in the east escaped unscathed. In fact cool and wet conditions helped field peas in the region, which should fare better than last year.
Drought-hit peas in the Beauce area had a yield of only 4.2-4.3 tonnes per hectare in 1996.
France produced 2.59 million tonnes of field peas for protein last year. The average yield was 4.83 tonnes per hectare.
